nodes.question: What type of data was processed to better understand LST hotspots in Athens?
nodes.answer: Satellite Euro-Mediterranean Journal for Environmental Integration time series data was processed.
nodes.paragraph: The mean spatial extent of SUHI in Athens was 55.2 km2, whilst its mean intensity was 5.6 C. This paper addresses this limitation by processing satellite Euro-Mediterranean Journal for Environmental Integration time series data to provide a more representative distribution of LST hotspots in a city, such as Athens, characterized by a dense and extensive urban sprawl. The poor air quality in cities has resulted in air pollu- tion being an important environmental stressor (Krefis et al. 2018). Evidence compiled from the last 20 years of research has clearly quantified health impacts not only in low- and middle-income countries where air pollution levels are high, but also in high-income countries with relatively clean air (EEA 2021). As a consequence, the latest release of WHO global air quality guidelines (WHO 2021) incorporates significant decreases in air pollution limits. Pollutant con- centrations from air quality monitoring stations have been widely used to derive hotspots of population exposure.
